Protecting your countrymen is a noble idea. However, free trade benefits your countryman in the aggregate more than tariffs would benefit the few of your countrymen who produce the product. Yes, tariffs help a few of your countrymen produce products at a higher price, but that higher price harms all of the countrymen who consume that product. The benefits of free-trade would be lowered costs paid for goods by the rest of your countrymen.

Tarriffs = hurting a majority of your countrymen to benefit a few of your countrymen. In the aggregate, the costs of higher prices actually harm your countrymen, not help them.

Example: using tariffs to help your countrymen who grow pineapples would benefit your pineapple growing countrymen but it would harm your pineapple-eating countrymen since they would now pay higher prices for pineapple, and in the end, consume less pineapples than they otherwise would have. In the aggregate, this would cost your the majority of your countrymen more money than it would save a few of your countrymen.

The only exception to this rule would be to protect industries necessary for the defense of your countrymen during war. So, adding tariffs to major food staples ensure that you can grow the food necessary to feed your troops, adding tariffs to energy production ensures you can produce your own fuel during war, adding tariffs to steel ensures that you can supply your tank factories during war, etc. All of these are necessary. But tariffs to protect the general businesses of your countrymen only serves to harm the rest of your countrymen. And in this latter case, the harm to the many outweighs the benefits to the few.
